questions.text: A regional economy has two states: State P (produces wheat, consumes sugar) and State Q (produces sugar, consumes wheat). Intermediaries facilitate trade. The government levies a 10% tax on all inter-state transactions and uses the revenue to subsidize transportation costs. In the circular flow model applied to this scenario, which of the following most accurately describes the government’s role?
options: It acts solely as a regulator setting trade rules between P and Q
It functions as both a participant (through taxation and subsidies) and a regulator of economic activity
It replaces intermediaries by directly handling transactions between states
It acts only as a consumer by purchasing wheat and sugar from both states
It operates outside the circular flow since taxes are external to trade
questions.correct_answer: It functions as both a participant (through taxation and subsidies) and a regulator of economic activity

questions.text: A market researcher collects the following data for a new snack product: At ₹10, 500 units are demanded; at ₹20, 300 units; at ₹30, 150 units. Suppliers offer 100 units at ₹10, 250 units at ₹20, and 400 units at ₹30. What is the approximate equilibrium price, and what happens if the government imposes a price ceiling of ₹15?
options: Equilibrium near ₹20; a ceiling at ₹15 creates a surplus since supply exceeds demand
Equilibrium near ₹20; a ceiling at ₹15 creates a shortage since demand exceeds supply at that price
Equilibrium near ₹30; a ceiling at ₹15 has no effect on the market
Equilibrium near ₹10; a ceiling at ₹15 creates a surplus
Equilibrium cannot be determined from this data
questions.correct_answer: Equilibrium near ₹20; a ceiling at ₹15 creates a shortage since demand exceeds supply at that price

questions.text: An analyst uses VLOOKUP to retrieve product prices from a master table. The lookup column (Product ID) has some duplicate entries with different prices due to regional variations. What problem will the analyst most likely encounter, and what is the best mitigation?
options: VLOOKUP will return an error; the analyst should use HLOOKUP instead
VLOOKUP will return the last matching value; sorting the table in descending order fixes this
VLOOKUP returns the first match it finds, which may not be the intended one; the analyst should ensure unique keys or use additional filtering
VLOOKUP will average all matching values automatically
VLOOKUP will return all matching values as an array
questions.correct_answer: VLOOKUP returns the first match it finds, which may not be the intended one; the analyst should ensure unique keys or use additional filtering

questions.text: A government agency wants to estimate monthly household consumption of fuel across India. The Census (conducted every 10 years) has comprehensive data but is outdated. CMIE’s Consumer Pyramids survey is available quarterly. Which data sourcing strategy best balances comprehensiveness with timeliness for this analysis?
options: Use only Census data since it covers the entire population
Use only CMIE data since it is more recent
Use Census data for structural demographic baselines and CMIE for recent consumption trends, cross-referencing both
Conduct a new full census specifically for fuel consumption
Use the Annual Survey of Industries since it covers industrial fuel use
questions.correct_answer: Use Census data for structural demographic baselines and CMIE for recent consumption trends, cross-referencing both

questions.text: A CMIE dataset shows that households in Southern India have higher EMI-to-income ratios than Northern India. The same data shows Southern states also have higher education expenditure and savings rates. Which inference is most reasonable from this data?
options: Southern households are financially irresponsible due to higher EMIs
Higher education levels in Southern states may correlate with greater financial product adoption and willingness to borrow for asset creation
Northern households save more because they avoid EMIs entirely
The data is contradictory since high EMIs should mean low savings
Southern households have higher incomes, fully explaining all three observations
questions.correct_answer: Higher education levels in Southern states may correlate with greater financial product adoption and willingness to borrow for asset creation

questions.text: A bank is estimating the addressable market for two-wheeler loans in a mid-sized city. Population: 5 lakh. 60% are aged 18+. RTO data shows 40% of adults have two-wheeler licenses. CMIE data suggests 30% of license holders intend to buy a new two-wheeler within 2 years. Average two- wheeler cost: ₹80,000. 70% of intending buyers opt for loans. What is the approximate total addressable loan market value?
options: ₹100.8 crore
₹50.4 crore
₹201.6 crore
₹33.6 crore
₹144 crore
questions.correct_answer: ₹201.6 crore

questions.text: A researcher studies two-wheeler buying intentions. She creates a 2x2 matrix: (Has FD / No FD) × (Owns two-wheeler / Doesn’t own). She finds that 45% of FD holders own two-wheelers vs. 30% of non-FD holders. Which statement best captures the analytical insight?
options: Having a fixed deposit causes people to buy two-wheelers
FD ownership shows positive correlation with two-wheeler ownership, suggesting financial stability may increase asset acquisition propensity, but causation cannot be established
Non-FD holders should be excluded from the target market entirely
The 15 percentage-point gap proves FD holders have higher income
The 2x2 matrix is inappropriate for this type of comparison
questions.correct_answer: FD ownership shows positive correlation with two-wheeler ownership, suggesting financial stability may increase asset acquisition propensity, but causation cannot be established

questions.text: An analyst creates a pivot table from student data with Department in Rows, Hostel in Columns, and Grade as Values (Count). She then adds a filter for ‘Computer Science’ only. The resulting table shows 5 hostels with varying grade distributions. If she now swaps Rows and Columns (Hostel in Rows, Department in Columns) while keeping the CS filter active, what happens?
options: The table becomes invalid since the filter conflicts with the column field
She sees 5 rows (hostels) with a single column (CS) showing grade counts per hostel
The pivot table automatically removes the filter
Each hostel row shows all departments, ignoring the filter
The table transposes but shows identical totals in a different arrangement
questions.correct_answer: She sees 5 rows (hostels) with a single column (CS) showing grade counts per hostel

questions.text: A data analyst has loan market share data for public banks, private banks, and NBFCs from 2015–2022. Market share changed significantly AND the total market size tripled during this period. Which chart type best communicates both the share shifts and the total market expansion simultaneously?
options: A standard pie chart for 2022 data only
A stacked area chart using absolute values (not percentages) to show both individual lender growth and total market expansion
A simple bar chart comparing only 2015 and 2022
A scatter plot of market share vs. total market size
Multiple pie charts, one for each year
questions.correct_answer: A stacked area chart using absolute values (not percentages) to show both individual lender growth and total market expansion

questions.text: A loan dataset shows: Lender X has average ticket size of ₹45,000 for two-wheeler loans and 15% market share. Lender Y has average ticket size of ₹38,000 and 25% market share. The total two- wheeler loan market is ₹10,000 crore. If Lender Y wants to match Lender X’s total loan value without changing its average ticket size, by approximately what percentage must it increase its number of loans?
options: It must increase by 18%
It must increase by 42%
It must increase by 29%
It must increase by 55%
It already exceeds Lender X’s total loan value due to its larger market share
questions.correct_answer: It already exceeds Lender X’s total loan value due to its larger market share

questions.text: An e-commerce company sees that its Beauty & Personal Care segment had 143.3% order volume growth (FY22 vs FY21), the highest among all categories. However, the segment’s overall retail share is only 2%, and traditional channels still hold 72.3% of that segment. Which strategic conclusion is most supported by this data?
options: The company should exit Beauty & Personal Care since its market size is too small
Traditional channels are dying in this segment given the high online growth
High growth rate on a small base represents an opportunity, but the large traditional channel share means significant offline competition remains
The 143.3% growth means this segment will soon overtake Food & Grocery in market size
The company should focus only on categories with over 50% online share
questions.correct_answer: High growth rate on a small base represents an opportunity, but the large traditional channel share means significant offline competition remains

questions.text: An online retailer manages 500 SKUs across three warehouses (H, C, M). Opening stock for SKU F01 is: H=391, C=77, M=50 (Total=518). Daily sales at warehouse C for the first 7 days of April: 10, 21, 15, 17, 13, 19, 15 units. What happens to warehouse C’s stock of F01 by the end of Day 7 (assuming no restocking), and what is the average daily demand rate?
options: 33 units remaining; average 6.3 units/day
Stock runs out during the week (stockout before Day 7); average demand is 15.7 units/day
0 units remaining; average 11 units/day
77 units remaining; no sales occurred
Cannot be determined without a replenishment schedule
questions.correct_answer: Stock runs out during the week (stockout before Day 7); average demand is 15.7 units/day

questions.text: ACE Gears produces Gear Assembly 3, which requires Gear 3-A (from Blank 011 via hobbing) and Gear 3-B (from Blank 021 via broaching). Blank 011 costs ₹105 and Blank 021 costs ₹35. The hobbing workstation produces 800 units/day on working days; broaching produces 780 units/day. If ACE Gears needs 4,000 units of Gear Assembly 3 in a month, what is the total raw material cost and which workstation is the production bottleneck?
options: ₹5,60,000; Hobbing is the bottleneck
₹5,60,000; Broaching is the bottleneck
₹4,20,000; Hobbing is the bottleneck
₹4,20,000; Broaching is the bottleneck
₹5,60,000; Neither is a bottleneck
questions.correct_answer: ₹5,60,000; Broaching is the bottleneck

questions.text: A manufacturing plant reports: Shift length = 8 hours (480 min), Breaks = 60 min, Downtime = 47 min, Ideal cycle time = 1.0 sec/unit, Total count = 19,271 units, Reject count = 423 units. What is the approximate Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE)?

In the ACE Gears scatter plot of Sales Quantity vs. Revenue, GA6 (BS4/6) appears as an outlier with very high volume but moderate revenue, while GA7 (BS4/6) shows high revenue but moderate volume. What is the most likely explanation for this pattern?
options: GA6 has a data entry error in its volume figures
GA6 is a low-priced, high-volume product while GA7 is a premium high-margin product, reflecting different pricing strategies
GA7 is less popular than GA6, so its data is unreliable
Both are outliers due to seasonal demand spikes and should be excluded from analysis
GA6 and GA7 use the same blanks, so their costs and pricing must be identical
questions.correct_answer: GA6 is a low-priced, high-volume product while GA7 is a premium high-margin product, reflecting different pricing strategies

questions.text: A company uses ABC classification for inventory. Item X: annual consumption ₹50 lakh (Category A). Item Y: ₹5 lakh (Category B). Item Z: ₹50,000 (Category C). Which inventory strategy combination is most appropriate?
options: X: EOQ with large batch orders; Y: JIT; Z: Safety stock
X: JIT with planned orders and accurate records; Y: Safety stock with planned orders; Z: EOQ with simple record-keeping
X: Safety stock; Y: EOQ; Z: JIT
All three should use JIT to minimize inventory holding costs
X: EOQ; Y: EOQ; Z: EOQ since all items need economic ordering
questions.correct_answer: X: JIT with planned orders and accurate records; Y: Safety stock with planned orders; Z: EOQ with simple record-keeping

questions.text: An HR team at a manufacturing firm needs to hire 50 new machine operators. Internal sourcing identifies 12 employees from the bench who can be retrained. The attrition rate for operators is 15% annually. How many external hires must the company make to net 50 additional operators after accounting for expected first-year attrition among the external hires?
options: 38 external hires
44 external hires
45 external hires (since 45 × 0.85 ≈ 38, plus 12 internal = 50)
50 external hires
Cannot determine without the onboarding success rate
questions.correct_answer: 45 external hires (since 45 × 0.85 ≈ 38, plus 12 internal = 50)

questions.text: A company runs an A/B test on its checkout page. Version A (control) shows a standard checkout. Version B adds a ‘Bought by 3 people in the last hour’ badge. After 2 weeks: Version B shows 4.5% conversion vs. A’s 3.1%. This scenario combines which two concepts from the course?
options: Market sizing and demand-supply equilibrium
A/B testing methodology and nudge theory (social proof as a behavioral nudge)
Credit risk assessment and A/B testing
Pivot table analysis and data visualization
VLOOKUP and conditional counting techniques
questions.correct_answer: A/B testing methodology and nudge theory (social proof as a behavioral nudge)

questions.text: A fintech company processes loan applications. A ₹5 lakh personal loan applicant: age 28, income ₹6 LPA, existing EMI ₹8,000/month, no prior defaults, but the PAN card submitted has a slightly different name spelling than the bank records. Under which credit risk category does the name mismatch primarily fall?
options: Eligibility risk - the applicant doesn’t meet income criteria
Fraud risk - the name mismatch suggests identity theft
Compliance risk - the KYC documents don’t match, creating regulatory issues
System issue - the automated system cannot process mismatched names
No risk - minor spelling differences are always irrelevant
questions.correct_answer: Compliance risk - the KYC documents don’t match, creating regulatory issues
